The curved line that starts at the origin and rises gently to the right is the **graph of the function y = √x**. It tells us that as x gets larger, its square root also gets larger, but the growth slows down (the curve flattens).

rows.said: what do the axes and the curve mean?
rows.reply:
The curved line is the set of points (x, √x); as x gets larger, its square‑root gets larger too, but more slowly—this is why the curve rises gently.

Now picture a square whose area is 9 square units. 
The length of each side of that square is the number that, when multiplied by itself, gives 9. That side length is the square root of 9.

The smooth curve that rises from the origin is the set of points \((x,\,\sqrt{x})\); as the input \(x\) gets bigger, the output \(y\) (the square root) also gets bigger, but more slowly.

What do you notice about how the curve moves as you go farther to the right?
